data_quote: [fire response: text, pdf p. 2] It is a fire sensitive obligate seeder, common in the understorey in heath and woodlands along the east coast and ranges of New South Wales, Australia (Weston 2002).; [primary_juvenile_period: abstract, pdf p. 1] The primary juvenile period of plants was 7-8 years, within the period of likely return fire intervals in the study area.; [age_at_first_flower_production_from_seed_repr3: text, pdf p. 5] No plants flowered until 6 years after the fire.; [site: text, pdf p. 2] We examined a population of *P. lanceolata* at one site within Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park 20 km north of Sydney (33°53' E, 151°13' S) southeastern Australia.; [rainfall: text, pdf p. 2] Annual precipitation for Sydney is around 1300 mm, while the average monthly maximum/minimum temperatures are 26/18 °C in summer and 16/8 °C in winter.; [fire: text, pdf p. 2] The site was burnt by an extensive summer (January) wildfire in 1994 that burnt all the surrounding habitat.
notes: primary_juvenile_period: first flowering 6 years after fire, first effective fruit set 7-8 years after fire, which the paper calls the primary juvenile period (pdf p. 6); age_at_first_flower_production_from_seed_repr3 is the time of first flowering (6 years); latitude and longitude: coordinates printed as '33°53' E, 151°13' S' with the labels swapped, read as latitude 33°53' s and longitude 151°13' e; rainfall_mm: printed 'around 1300 mm', annual precipitation for sydney; fire_season_categorical: printed 'summer (january)'; site previously burnt in a summer wildfire 15 years before 1994
source: auld, t. d., denham, a. j., & turner, k. (2007). dispersal and recruitment dynamics in the fleshy-fruited persoonia lanceolata (proteaceae).

data_quote: [fire response: text, p. 42] This study indicates that *S. garlandii* is principally a seeder although some plants function as sprouters after a low-intensity fire.; [resprouter type: text, p. 39] While the fire killed many of the existing *Senecio* plants some survived by resprouting from a rootstock.; [site: text, p. 36] At only 340 ha, The Rock Nature Reserve (lat. 35° 16' S, long. 147° 05' E) is a small island of remnant native vegetation, surrounded by extensive agricultural lands.; [fire: text, p. 36] After less than 75 mm of rain during November 1990 to March 1991 (average 208 mm for this period) the first major fire (15–17 March 1991) in 40 years burnt more than 90% of The Rock Nature Reserve (personal observation).; [post-fire rainfall: text, p. 43] This suggests that a low fire intensity, combined with more than the about 25 mm of rainfall received in the 2.5 months after the March fire (Fig. 2), then more *Senecio* rootstocks may have resprouted.

data_quote: [fire response: abstract, pdf p. 1] We hypothesised increased time to maturity and decreased serotinous seed stores available for post-fire recruitment due to declining rainfall over recent decades for two fire-killed serotinous shrubs of south-east Australian MTEs, *Hakea decurrens* and *Banksia ornata*.; [time_to_50_percent_flowering: text, pdf p. 6] Although cones were first present at 3 years TSF for both periods, probability of reproductive maturity was 50% at 3 years and 90% by 14 years TSF in the 1990s but did not reach comparable levels until 15 years and 26 years TSF, respectively, in 2017, representing a 12-year delay; [site and sample size: text, pdf p. 5] We surveyed 842 *H. decurrens* plants in Grampians NP; 444 individuals from six stand ages in the 1990s, and 398 from six stand ages in 2017.; [rainfall: methods, pdf p. 5] estimated annual rainfall values using the TerraClimate northern Grampians mean of 630 mm per year
